summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 100-1400 views there, while YouTube Shorts barely gets any (mostly under 30 views). The best video by far is the PIR motion sensor one, which opened with a surprising claim and a question about a device people see every day. Smoke alarm, street light and IR sensor videos did okay on Instagram but get few likes, shares or saves, so viewers watch but don't engage much. The English Arduino video is the only one getting real YouTube views (160), but it has no Instagram numbers, so it's too early to say English is better.
winningPattern: Everyday 'how does it know?' sensor subjects (PIR, street light, auto door, tap) with a shock-style Hindi hook that says the device does NOT do the obvious thing (e.g. 'Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!'), followed by a short curious question title with the 🤔 emoji. It works best on Instagram Reels, where reach is 5-10x higher than YouTube.
doMore: Open every title and first line with a surprising 'it does NOT do X' claim, like the PIR video
Pick sensors people meet daily (lifts, ATM, AC, fan, car parking beep) and ask how it knows
Post Reels on Instagram first and treat it as the main platform for now
End each video with a clear ask to share or save (e.g. 'Dost ko bhejo jo sochta hai ye magic hai')
Test 2-3 English or Hinglish videos on both platforms to see if YouTube grows with them
stopDoing: Making near-duplicate topics (two smoke alarm videos in 3 days) that split the audience
Using generic titles without a shock claim, like 'Touchscreen Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' style plain questions
Judging YouTube performance from Hindi uploads alone without testing different hooks or language
nextTopics: Lift knows which floor you pressed and when to stop
